# ui-locate-mcp
**English** · 简体中文
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ui-locate-mcp) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
Find on-screen UI text locally and return pixel coordinates for desktop interaction. Combined tools
can locate, click, type, scroll and attempt to verify the result.
Detection, OCR and actions run locally. Initial setup downloads Python dependencies and a detection
model of about 80 MB. A persistent service runs inference; a lightweight MCP process forwards reques
el of about 80 MB. A persistent service runs inference; a lightweight MCP process forwards requests.
## Quick start

1. Enter `ui-locate-mcp` in DSH **Plugins → Add plugin**, then enable it.
2. Open **ui-locate runtim
e** in Settings, choose paths and a backend, and prepare the environment. The Host tool `ui_locate_s

etup` provides the same preparation path.
3. After preparation, connect or re-enable `mcp-ui-locate`

. Restart if DSH requests it.
4. Call `health`, then try `locate_text(text="Save")`.
The bundle contains an MCP client, a Host runtime-management plugin and a Client settings page. npm
installation supplies the code; Python dependencies and the model require separate setup.
### Requirements
- The current bundle's MCP executable path is configured for **Windows**. Cross-platform Python code

does not imply a cross-platform bundle configuration.
- The Python project requires **Python 3.12+*
*. The settings preparation uses a Python runtime located by the host to create a dedicated environm

ent. Check the desktop installation's bundled runtime if no interpreter can be found.
- **DirectML**
is the default backend; `cuda` and `cpu` are alternatives. CUDA needs the corresponding NVIDIA envi

ronment and larger dependencies. Changing backends requires rebuilding the environment.
- package.js
on currently declares no `engines.dsh` range. This is not a guarantee of compatibility with every DS
H version: the bundle needs tool registration, an MCP client and settings services.

| Tool | Purpose |

| `locate_text` | Find matching UI text and its center coordinates |
| `find_all` | Return multiple

matching candidates |
| `detect_elements` | Enumerate detected elements |
| `ui_locate_marks` | Scre
enshot with numbered marks (and an optional named grid) so the model picks a number instead of guess

ing pixels |
| `ui_locate_act` | Locate, perform an action and attempt verification |
| `ui_locate_s

teps` | Run ordered steps and identify failures |
| `ui_locate_windows` | List top-level windows (ti

tle, handle, client rect, foreground) |
| `ui_locate_diff` | Where the screen changed since the last

call, as rectangles (no image, no vision tokens) |

Besides detector boxes, marks include repeated same-size cells found by geometry alone (inventory sl
ots, tabs, skill bars, tables; `kind: "cell"`), which UI detectors usually miss in games. Numbers be
long to one marked image; pass `mark_set` to refuse a stale one.
Coordinates are absolute screen coordinates and may be negative on secondary displays. `monitor` acc
epts `primary`, an index string, `all`, `window:<title>` or `hwnd:<handle>`. Locate again after the
mary`, an index string, `all`, `window:<title>` or `hwnd:<handle>`. Locate again after the UI moves.
### Working with one window
Pass `window=` (title or part of it, or a handle) to `ui_locate_marks`, `ui_locate_act` or `ui_locat
ndow=` (title or part of it, or a handle) to `ui_locate_marks`, `ui_locate_act` or `ui_locate_diff`:
- Capture tries Windows Graphics Capture first: it reads the window from the compositor, so a game c
overed by the chat window is still captured, GPU-rendered content included, cropped to the client ar
ea. One session per window stays open while frames are being requested (closed after 15 s idle), so
repeated grabs during watch/wait are nearly free. If WGC fails or returns black it falls back to `Pr
intWindow`, then to cropping a monitor capture. `UI_LOCATE_WINDOW_CAPTURE` / `"window_capture"`: `au
to` (default), `wgc`, `printwindow`, `screen`. WGC needs the `windows-capture` package; the plugin i
nstalls it with `--no-deps` (its metadata asks for `opencv-python`, which clashes with `opencv-pytho
n-headless`). On Windows 10 a yellow capture border may show around the window; Windows 11 turns it

off.
- Before sending input, the target window is brought to the foreground (SendInput only reaches
the foreground window). Without `window=`, mouse actions focus the window under the point; `focus="o

ff"` disables it. `performed.focus` reports whether it worked.
- Marks taken with `window=` keep it,
so `ui_locate_act(mark=…)` later focuses and verifies that window.
